concepts.concept: Spinlock state (the 32-bit lock file)  the stored per-index lock bits that the module keeps and reports
concepts.writers: Reset: lock_q(i) <= '0' when rstn_i = '0' (line 42). Update: on rising_edge(clk_i) (line 43) when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') and (sel(i) = '1') then lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw (lines 44-45), written from the bus_req_i inputs via the spinlock process.
concepts.observers: bus_rsp_o.data is driven from lock_q and sel at line 68 (bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel) when addr(7) = '0' and from lock_q at line 70 (bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q) when addr(7) <> '0' (lines 68 and 70), exposing lock bits on the bus response.

confidentiality.reason: lock_q holds bits written from bus_req_i and those bits are returned on bus_rsp_o.data (e.g. bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel at line 68 and bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q at line 70), so an external master can read them and secrecy depends on integration.

integrity.reason: lock_q is written from bus_req_i (lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw at line 45 under the guard at line 44) and these bits implement locks used on readback (lines 68/70), so external bus writes can change protection state.

availability.reason: writes to lock_q occur only when (bus_req_i.stb = '1') and address decode matches (guard at line 44), so an external requester controlling bus_req_i.stb/addr can block or force updates and prevent progress.

undermined behavior.reason: lock_q has only the reset assignment (line 42) and the spinlock process assignment (line 45) as drivers and there is no debug/test override or alternate assignment path.

concepts.concept: Address-to-index decode decision (sel)  which lock bit index a bus request targets
concepts.writers: sel(i) is computed combinationally from the address: sel(i) <= '1' when (bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) = std_ulogic_vector(to_unsigned(i, 5))) else '0' (line 51); sel has no storage (combinational driven by bus_req_i.addr).
concepts.observers: sel influences bus_rsp_o.data via the masked read at line 68 (bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel) and controls which bit is returned; sel itself is derived from the external address input (line 51).

confidentiality.reason: sel is purely derived from the external bus_req_i.addr (line 51) that the requester supplies, so it reveals nothing beyond what the requester already knows.

integrity.reason: sel is computed from bus_req_i.addr at line 51 and is used to gate writes (line 44) and mask readback (line 68), so corruption or malicious control of the address input can mis-target accesses and integrity depends on trust in the bus source.

availability.reason: sel is a combinational decode of bus_req_i.addr (line 51), so an external master can choose addresses that prevent some indices from being selected and thereby block access to those locks.

undermined behavior.reason: sel is driven only by the address decode at line 51 and there is no alternate debug/test override or bypass for the decode.
